title:
一、英譯中：請將下列英文句子譯成中文。（15 分）
“We are true to our creed when a little girl born into the bleakest poverty knows that she has the same chance to succeed as anybody else…” Barack Obama, inaugural address, 2013
answer: 「當一個出生於最陰暗貧困之中的小女孩，知道自己和其他任何人一樣有成功的機會時，我們才算忠於自己的信念……」——巴拉克·歐巴馬，2013 年就職演說
hint:
句構拆解
  • We are true to our creed when...：be true to＝忠於；creed＝信念、信條；when 引導時間副詞子句（當……時）。
  • a little girl born into the bleakest poverty：born into 是過去分詞片語修飾 a little girl（出生於……）；bleakest＝最陰暗、最荒涼的（bleak 的最高級）。
  • knows that she has the same chance to succeed as anybody else：that 子句；the same... as...＝與……相同的……。
關鍵詞
  • be true to one's creed 忠於信念
  • born into poverty 出生於貧困
  • the bleakest poverty 最陰暗的貧困
  • the same chance to succeed as anybody else 與其他人一樣的成功機會
翻譯技巧
  • 英文先講「我們忠於信念」，再說「當……時」；中文習慣把條件放前面：「當……時，我們才算忠於信念」。
  • bleakest 直譯「最荒涼的」不適合修飾 poverty，譯「最陰暗的貧困」或「赤貧」。
  • 這是演說引文，語氣要正式、有節奏；句末用刪節號保留原文的未完感。
易錯點
  • 把 creed 譯成「教條」——此處是「信念、信條」。
  • 把 born into 譯成「被生進」——中文說「出生於」。

title:
二、中譯英：請將下列中文句子譯成英文。（15 分）
正如同被水包圍的魚不知道已全身濕透，被媒體包圍的大眾，他們對世界的看法不知不覺也被影響。
answer: Just as a fish surrounded by water does not know that it is soaking wet, the public surrounded by the media are unconsciously influenced in how they see the world.
hint:
句構策略
  • 「正如同 A，B」→ Just as A, B（A、B 兩個子句對稱）。
  • 「被水包圍的魚」→ a fish surrounded by water（過去分詞片語後位修飾）。
  • 「不知道已全身濕透」→ does not know that it is soaking wet（soaking wet＝濕透）。
  • 「被媒體包圍的大眾」→ the public surrounded by the media。
  • 「對世界的看法不知不覺也被影響」→ are unconsciously influenced in how they see the world。
關鍵詞
  • 正如同 just as
  • 包圍 surround／be surrounded by
  • 濕透 soaking wet／drenched
  • 大眾 the public（集合名詞，動詞可用複數 are）
  • 不知不覺 unconsciously／without realizing it
  • 對世界的看法 how they see the world／their view of the world
加分寫法
  • 也可用 In the same way that... 代替 Just as。
  • 「看法被影響」可用 their perception of the world is shaped without their awareness，更書面。
易錯點
  • the public 當主詞時，英式用法常接複數動詞 are，美式可接單數 is；本句用 are 較自然。
  • 「不知不覺」不要譯成 don't know——那是「不知道」，不是「無意識地」。

title:
三、英文作文：（20 分）
In a composition of no less than 200 words, name the most useful quality with which a millennial can thrive in the 21st century and offer your reasons why you think so.
answer:
If I had to name one quality that will decide whether a millennial thrives in this century, I would not choose intelligence or ambition. I would choose adaptability—the willingness to unlearn what no longer works and learn what does.

The first reason is the speed of change. The jobs that exist today did not exist twenty years ago, and many of them will be automated within twenty. A graduate who defines herself by a single skill is betting that the world will stand still. Someone who treats her career as a series of experiments can move from industry to industry without losing momentum.

The second reason is that adaptability protects against failure. Millennials entered the workforce during a financial crisis, watched a pandemic rewrite office life, and now face artificial intelligence that can write, draw, and code. None of these disruptions were predictable. The people who recovered fastest were not the most talented; they were the ones who could absorb a shock, rethink their assumptions, and try again.

Finally, adaptability is a habit that can be learned. Reading outside one's field, taking short courses, asking naive questions, and volunteering for unfamiliar projects all train the same muscle. It costs little and compounds over time.

Intelligence opens a door, and ambition pushes you through it. But adaptability is what keeps you in the room when the room itself keeps changing.
hint:
審題
  • 題目要求選出一項特質（name the most useful quality），並說明理由；不可列一堆特質。
  • 建議主題：adaptability（適應力），最貼合千禧世代面對的快速變動。
  • 其他可選：resilience（韌性）、curiosity（好奇心）、digital literacy（數位素養）、empathy（同理心）。
五段架構
  • 第一段（引言）：先排除 intelligence／ambition，再點出 adaptability，並給一句定義（unlearn＋learn）。
  • 第二段（理由一：變化速度）：現在的工作二十年前不存在，二十年後可能被自動化；單一技能是賭世界不變。
  • 第三段（理由二：抗失敗）：金融危機、疫情、AI——三波衝擊都無法預測，適應力強的人恢復最快。
  • 第四段（理由三：可學習）：跨領域閱讀、短期課程、問笨問題、接下陌生專案，都是可訓練的。
  • 第五段（結論）：intelligence 開門、ambition 推你進去，但 adaptability 讓你在不斷改變的房間裡留下來。
關鍵詞彙
  • adaptability 適應力；unlearn 拋棄舊知
  • automate 自動化；disruption 顛覆性衝擊
  • momentum 動能；assumption 預設
  • compound over time 隨時間累積
加分句型
  • If I had to name one quality..., I would not choose... I would choose...（假設語氣破題）
  • A graduate who defines herself by a single skill is betting that the world will stand still.（比喻）
  • Intelligence opens a door, and ambition pushes you through it. But adaptability is what keeps you in the room...（三段式收尾）
評分重點
  • 必須明確點名一項特質，並在每段回扣。
  • 理由要具體（自動化、疫情、AI），不要只說「很重要」。
  • 字數至少 200 字，建議 230–260 字。

title: Doctor Wong is promoted because he has done an excellent job of supervising the medical ______.
hint:
1. Doctor Wong is promoted because he has done an excellent job of supervising the medical laboratory.
（黃醫師獲得升遷，因為他在督導醫學實驗室方面表現優異。）
  • 考點：laboratory＝實驗室；medical laboratory＝醫學實驗室。
  • 線索：Doctor（醫師）＋supervising（督導）＋medical（醫學的）→ 醫學實驗室。
  • 其他選項：catalogue 目錄；compliment 讚美；segment 部分。
撇步
  • 醫師督導的單位 → medical laboratory。

title: Without receiving final approval from its board of trustees, the university has ______ set its budget for the next academic year at NT$200 million.
hint:
2. Without receiving final approval from its board of trustees, the university has tentatively set its budget for the next academic year at NT$200 million.
（在尚未獲得董事會最終批准的情況下，該校暫定下學年度預算為新臺幣兩億元。）
  • 考點：tentatively＝暫定地、暫時地（形容詞 tentative）。
  • 線索：Without receiving final approval（尚未獲得最終批准）→ 所以只是「暫定」。
  • 其他選項：beneficially 有益地；passionately 熱烈地；reliably 可靠地。
撇步
  • 未定案、待批准 → tentatively；定案才是 finally。

title: After being interrogated by the police for two days, the suspect finally ______ to the crime.
hint:
3. After being interrogated by the police for two days, the suspect finally confessed to the crime.
（被警方偵訊兩天後，嫌犯終於認罪。）
  • 考點：confess to＝承認、認罪（to 為介系詞，後接名詞）。
  • 線索：interrogated（偵訊）＋suspect（嫌犯）→ 認罪。
  • 其他選項：authorize 授權；discipline 懲戒；improvise 即興。
撇步
  • 認罪、承認 → confess (to)；注意 to 是介系詞。

title: It is believed that the ______ have been living on Austronesian (Southern Asian) Islands for thousands of years.
hint:
4. It is believed that the aborigines have been living on Austronesian (Southern Asian) Islands for thousands of years.
（一般認為原住民族已在南島（東南亞）群島居住數千年。）
  • 考點：aborigines＝原住民（澳洲、台灣等原住民族）；此處指南島語族原住民。
  • 線索：for thousands of years（數千年）→ 最早居住的一群人＝原住民。
  • 其他選項：assistants 助理；newcomers 新來者；sponsors 贊助者。
撇步
  • 住了數千年 → aborigines（原住民）。

title: One of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's top officials arrived at the United States where he is expected to help ______ the groundwork for talks between Kim and US President in Singapore.
hint:
5. ...where he is expected to help lay the groundwork for talks between Kim and US President in Singapore.
（他預計將協助為金正恩與美國總統在新加坡的會談奠定基礎。）
  • 考點：lay the groundwork for＝為……奠定基礎（固定搭配）；lay 的過去式/過去分詞是 laid。
  • 辨析：lay（放置，及物）vs lie（躺，不及物）；raise（舉起，及物）vs rise（上升，不及物）。
  • 其他選項：lie、rise 都不及物，不能接 the groundwork。
撇步
  • 「奠定基礎」＝lay the groundwork / lay the foundation。

title: In 2010, a South Korean couple was    6    the murder of their daughter through neglect. When their daughter was born, she weighed 2.9 kilograms. Three months later, when she    7   , she weighed 2.4 kilograms. The strangest part was that the parents were playing a game for many hours each day in which they raised a    8    child online. Similarly, in 2014, a young South Korean man who spent much of his time in Internet Cafés was arrested after his two-year-old son starved to death. South Korea has seen exponential growth in computer and Internet use. This has caused many to worry that certain users are    9    unable to control how much time they spend on the Internet. They fear an epidemic of addiction to video game. South Korea is not    10   : many other developed countries have also experienced huge growth in video games and Internet addiction.

subItems.hint:
6. In 2010, a South Korean couple was charged with the murder of their daughter through neglect.
（2010 年，一對韓國夫妻因疏於照顧致死而被控謀殺女兒。）
  • 考點：be charged with＝被控告（某罪）。
  • 線索：the murder（謀殺）→ 被「起訴、控告」。
  • 其他選項：change into 變成；choose from 從中選擇；check out 檢查、退房。
撇步
  • 被控某罪＝be charged with / be accused of。

7. Three months later, when she passed away, she weighed 2.4 kilograms.
（三個月後她過世時，體重只有 2.4 公斤。）
  • 考點：pass away＝去世（委婉語）。
  • 線索：體重從 2.9 公斤掉到 2.4 公斤＋謀殺案 → 女嬰已死亡。
  • 其他選項：break down 故障、崩潰；run out 用完；start over 重新開始。
撇步
  • 死亡委婉語：pass away / pass on。

8. ...the parents were playing a game for many hours each day in which they raised a virtual child online.
（……這對父母每天花好幾小時玩一款在線上養育虛擬小孩的遊戲。）
  • 考點：virtual＝虛擬的；virtual child＝虛擬小孩。
  • 線索：playing a game（玩遊戲）＋online（線上）→ 虛擬的。
  • 其他選項：crucial 關鍵的；visual 視覺的；racial 種族的。
撇步
  • 線上、遊戲、模擬 → virtual（virtual reality 虛擬實境）。

9. This has caused many to worry that certain users are increasingly unable to control how much time they spend on the Internet.
（這讓許多人擔心，某些使用者越來越無法控制自己上網的時間。）
  • 考點：increasingly＝越來越（修飾 unable）。
  • 線索：exponential growth（指數型成長）→ 問題「越來越」嚴重。
  • 其他選項：spaciously 寬敞地；simultaneously 同時地；interestingly 有趣地。
撇步
  • 程度持續加深 → increasingly + adj.。

10. South Korea is not alone: many other developed countries have also experienced huge growth in video games and Internet addiction.
（韓國並不孤單：許多其他已開發國家也經歷了電玩與網路成癮的大幅成長。）
  • 考點：not alone＝並非只有它一個、並不孤單（後面用 also 呼應）。
  • 線索：many other developed countries have also...（其他國家也……）→ 韓國「不是唯一」。
  • 其他選項：not over 尚未結束；not all 並非全部；not new 不新。
撇步
  • 後句出現 also／too → 前句用 not alone。

title:
Until the late 1700s, the economy of England was tightly controlled by the government, which limited the amount of interest that banks could charge, laid down rules about how employers should treat their workers, and set strict standards for how some products should be made. The government set up trade monopolies, giving certain companies the sole right to trade with certain parts of the world, like the English East India Company.    11    Then in the late 1700s, Adam Smith published a book called The Wealth of Nations, which advocated “laissez-faire,” meaning “to let alone” in French.    12    He said individuals should be left alone to make their own economic decisions—what products to make, how to make them, and what to charge for them.    13    People would be motivated by the opportunity to try new ideas and make more money. Society, as a result, would become wealthier.

After Smith's book was published, the idea of laissez-faire became more and more popular.    14    The new freedom to invent and invest helped spur the Industrial Revolution, creating, as Adam Smith had predicted, vast new wealth.

But it also created the harsh conditions some employers maintained in the factories. These employers were believers in laissez-faire.    15    They say it was none of the government's business how much their workers were paid or how many hours a day they worked. For obvious reasons, the idea of laissez-faire was more popular among employers than among their workers.

options.text: They fought against laws that would make things better for workers.
In the book Smith argued government controls were hurting the economy.
This economic freedom, he believed, would make people more creative and hard-working.
To protect English manufacturers, the government set high tariffs on goods imported from foreign countries.

subItems.hint:
11. → To protect English manufacturers, the government set high tariffs on goods imported from foreign countries.
（為了保護英國製造商，政府對外國進口商品課徵高關稅。）
  • 定位：空格前在描述政府如何嚴密控制經濟（限制利率、規定雇主、設貿易壟斷），空格後接「然後在 1700 年代末，亞當·史密斯出版……」→ 空格應再補一個政府控制經濟的例子。
  • 選項契合：「課徵高關稅」正是政府干預市場的典型手段，與前面的 monopoly、rules 並列。
  • 其他選項：they fought（勞工法）、in the book（史密斯的書）、this economic freedom（自由）都不合「政府控制」的語境。
撇步
  • 篇章結構先看空格前後的主題：此處主題是「政府控制」，就選控制手段。

options.text: They fought against laws that would make things better for workers.
In the book Smith argued government controls were hurting the economy.
This economic freedom, he believed, would make people more creative and hard-working.
To protect English manufacturers, the government set high tariffs on goods imported from foreign countries.

subItems.hint:
12. → In the book Smith argued government controls were hurting the economy.
（史密斯在書中主張，政府管制正在傷害經濟。）
  • 定位：前句介紹《國富論》提倡 laissez-faire（放任）；後句「He said individuals should be left alone...」→ 空格應說明書中的主張。
  • 選項契合：「政府管制傷害經濟」正好承接「放任」的主張，並開啟下一句「個人應被放任」。
  • 其他選項：關稅（政府的做法）、this economic freedom（後續才談）、they fought（勞工）都不合。
撇步
  • 看到前句提到「一本書」，空格常是該書的論點。

options.text: Many of the old laws controlling the economy were abolished.
They fought against laws that would make things better for workers.
This economic freedom, he believed, would make people more creative and hard-working.
In the book Smith argued government controls were hurting the economy.

subItems.hint:
13. → This economic freedom, he believed, would make people more creative and hard-working.
（他相信這種經濟自由會讓人們更有創造力、更勤奮。）
  • 定位：前句「He said individuals should be left alone to make their own economic decisions...」＋後句「People would be motivated by the opportunity to try new ideas and make more money.」→ 空格應承接「自由」並帶出「人會更有動力」。
  • 選項契合：This economic freedom 指涉前句的放任，「more creative and hard-working」對應後句的 motivated。
  • 其他選項：old laws abolished（後續才發生）、they fought（勞工）、in the book（已講過）。
撇步
  • 代名詞線索：This economic freedom 一定緊接在「經濟自由」之後。

options.text: Many of the old laws controlling the economy were abolished.
They fought against laws that would make things better for workers.
In the book Smith argued government controls were hurting the economy.
This economic freedom, he believed, would make people more creative and hard-working.

subItems.hint:
14. → Many of the old laws controlling the economy were abolished.
（許多控制經濟的舊法律被廢除。）
  • 定位：前句「laissez-faire 的想法越來越受歡迎」；後句「The new freedom to invent and invest helped spur the Industrial Revolution...」→ 空格應說明舊法被廢除，才會有「新的自由」。
  • 選項契合：abolished（廢除）正好承接 popular，並導出 the new freedom。
  • 其他選項：they fought（勞工抗爭，屬下一段）、in the book（已講過）、this economic freedom（已用於 13）。
撇步
  • 空格後出現 the new freedom → 前面一定是「舊限制被解除」。

options.text: Many of the old laws controlling the economy were abolished.
They fought against laws that would make things better for workers.
In the book Smith argued government controls were hurting the economy.
This economic freedom, he believed, would make people more creative and hard-working.

subItems.hint:
15. → They fought against laws that would make things better for workers.
（他們反對那些會改善勞工處境的法律。）
  • 定位：前句「These employers were believers in laissez-faire.」；後句「They say it was none of the government's business how much their workers were paid...」→ 空格主詞 They＝employers，動作應是反對改善勞工的法律。
  • 選項契合：They fought against laws 與後句 They say 主詞一致、語意連貫。
  • 其他選項：old laws abolished（已用於 14）、in the book（已用）、this economic freedom（已用）。
撇步
  • 篇章結構常見線索：代名詞 They 指誰——此處指前句的 employers。

title:
Just as a passport represents national sovereignty—it is one of the defining categories of a claim to statehood—so harmonizing passports is a sign of cooperation. That can be a slow process. It took the nine members of the-then European Community (now the 27-strong European Union) years to settle on the color of the passport cover that its member states now share. In 1976, a year after a uniform passport was first proposed, Britain shuddered at the suggested shade of delicate lilac. Diplomats then spent four years dismissing maroon and then purple before reaching a wine-colored consensus in 1981.

America's first passport cover, in 1918, was beige, going green three years later. It changed to various shades of red in 1926 and back to green in 1941. Only on the bicentenary in 1976 did it turn blue, matching the shade in the American flag.

The common color was supposed to make European passports instantly recognizable. But since colors cannot be patented, nothing stops others with the same idea. Some countries that hoped to join the EU quickly adopted the right color of passport as a branding exercise. In South America the Andean Community, which once had EU-like aspirations, also favors wine-colored passports. Mercosur and Caricom, two other regional groupings, favor an American-style dark blue.

Countries commonly pick colors that reflect their culture or religion, says Claire Burrows of De La Rue, a British company that has been making passports since 1915. Islamic countries often have green passport covers (though Germany's passport used to be that color, as are those of members of the Economic Community of West African States). According to Bill Waldron of Holliston, a Tennessee-based firm that prints documents for 65 of the world's 249 passport-issuing entities, darker colors are popular because they show dirt less, heighten the contrast with the crest and look more official—much as police wear dark uniforms.

Interpol—one of a handful of international organizations with passport-issuing powers—provides evidence for that theory: its new travel document is black. The UN's passport, like the helmets of its peacekeeping force, is a pacific blue.

Fun-colored passports exist too. But they can sometimes seem a punishment: Sweden and the Netherlands issue emergency travel documents for nationals who have lost their passports. They are pink.

subItems.title: 16. According to the passage, which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.text: In 1918, the passport color was beige in the US.
In 1930, the US used burgundy covers for their passports.
From 1941 to 1976, US travelers were issued burgundy passports.
The color of US passport changed to blue as its 200th anniversary was marked.

subItems.hint:
→ From 1941 to 1976, US travelers were issued burgundy passports.
（下列何者不為真？→ 1941 至 1976 年美國護照是酒紅色。）
  • 定位：第二段「It changed to various shades of red in 1926 and back to green in 1941. Only on the bicentenary in 1976 did it turn blue.」
  • 推論：1941 年已改回綠色，1976 年才變藍——所以 1941–1976 是綠色，不是酒紅色，C 錯誤。
  • 其他選項：(A) 1918 米色 ✓；(B) 1930 落在 1926 年起的紅色時期 ✓；(D) 1976 建國兩百週年變藍 ✓。
撇步
  • 時間軸題把年份排成一列：1918 米→1921 綠→1926 紅→1941 綠→1976 藍。

subItems.title: 17. Which of the following countries use the same color for their passports?
subItems.hint:
→ Liberia and Pakistan.
（下列哪兩國護照顏色相同？→ 賴比瑞亞與巴基斯坦。）
  • 定位：第四段「Islamic countries often have green passport covers... as are those of members of the Economic Community of West African States.」
  • 推論：巴基斯坦是伊斯蘭國家（綠）；賴比瑞亞是西非國家經濟共同體成員（綠）→ 兩者皆綠。
  • 其他選項：秘魯（安地斯共同體、酒紅）vs 美國（藍）；英國（曾酒紅，現藍）vs 沙烏地（綠）；西班牙（歐盟酒紅）vs 奈及利亞（西非綠）。
撇步
  • 這題需要背景知識＋文中線索：伊斯蘭國家、西非共同體都是綠色。

subItems.title: 18. Which of the following about the meanings of passport colors is NOT mentioned in the passage?
subItems.hint:
→ Emphasizing their national sovereignty.
（關於護照顏色的意義，下列何者未在文中提及？→ 強調國家主權。）
  • 定位：文中提到顏色反映 culture or religion（第四段）、與 國旗同色（美國藍，第二段）。
  • 陷阱：第一段雖說「護照代表國家主權」，但那是護照本身的意義，不是「顏色」的意義。
  • 其他選項：文化、宗教、國旗都在文中被明確連結到顏色。
撇步
  • 注意題目問的是「顏色的意義」——主權是全本護照的意義，不是顏色。

subItems.title: 19. According to the passage, why do passports normally come in dark shades?

options.text: To show patriotism and respect their own history.
To coordinate with passports of other countries.
To look formal in the international arena.
To fit in with the multicultural world.

subItems.hint:
→ To look formal in the international arena.
（為什麼護照多用深色？→ 在國際場合看起來正式。）
  • 定位：第四段「darker colors are popular because they show dirt less, heighten the contrast with the crest and look more official—much as police wear dark uniforms.」
  • 推論：look more official＝看起來更正式、更有官方感，對應 (C)。
  • 其他選項：愛國、與他國協調、多元文化——都不是文中理由。
撇步
  • 因果題找 because：show dirt less / contrast / look more official。

subItems.title: 20. What does the word “Interpol” possibly refer to?
subItems.hint:
→ International Criminal Police Organization.
（Interpol 可能指什麼？→ 國際刑警組織。）
  • 定位：第五段「Interpol—one of a handful of international organizations with passport-issuing powers...」
  • 背景知識：Interpol 是 International Criminal Police Organization 的簡稱（國際刑警組織）。
  • 其他選項：安地斯共同體（CAN）、APEC、OPEC 都是不同組織。
撇步
  • 縮寫題：先把全名唸出來對照——International Criminal Police。

title:
When contemporary women writers write about mother-daughter relationships, they often put an emphasis on forging a connection between them. In their writing, even though mothers and daughters do have ambivalence toward each other, they are often capable of resolving this problem and finally recognizing their bond as mothers and daughters. Yet, when it comes to writing about mother-son relationships, it becomes a completely different story. Most women writers stress the alienation between mothers and sons owing to the fact that they are of different gender. Therefore, when women writers write about their experiences of raising sons, they usually find themselves crossing over into a different territory. Feelings of apprehension and distress arise when mothers discover to their astonishment that their sons have become a total stranger to them especially when the sons have stepped into adulthood. In addition, since mothers are constrained by the society at large to avoid being too close to their sons in fear that they might smother their sons, contemporary women writers have depicted mostly the separation between them but have also unveiled how mothers come to terms with this separation from their sons.

Take the two contemporary novels, Margaret Forster's Mothers' Boys and Rosellen Brown's Before and After, as examples. With a common theme on mother-son relationships, both novels portray a similar incident of a son who is suspected of committing a murder and how this unexpected event has profoundly harmed the mother-son relationships. Coincidently, both novels have an identical scene with a mother-son encounter in a juvenile prison. In this confrontation between mothers and sons, mothers have to their bewilderment come to realize that their sons have become unknown to them. And as these mother-son narratives continue to develop, the mothers and sons in these novels finally separate from each other. The only difference between these novels is their contrast in treating the mother-son relationship. Forster presents the mother as the one who takes up her traditional role by accepting passively this separation from son and waiting patiently until the son returns one day whereas Brown describes a mother who exercises her agency and power to deal with her son's act of crime. Later, she not only fulfills her social responsibility as a mother but also decides her way of handling the mother-son separation. Despite that the two texts illustrate two conflicting ways of reading and writing mother-son relationships, they also inform us that there exists a powerful reading and writing against the grain.

subItems.title: 21. Which field of study is most closely related to this passage?
subItems.hint:
→ Women's Studies.
（本文與哪個研究領域最相關？→ 女性研究。）
  • 定位：全篇談「contemporary women writers 如何書寫母女、母子關係」，核心是女性作家的書寫與性別視角。
  • 其他選項：人力資源、社會工作、人權——都不是本文的學科脈絡。
撇步
  • 領域題看重複出現的主體：women writers、mothers、gender。

subItems.title: 22. According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about the mother-son relationship?

options.text: Mothers find it hard to discipline their sons.
Sons express less filial piety to their mothers.
Mothers sense great indifference from their sons.
Sons have strong anxiety over being mothers' boys.

subItems.hint:
→ Mothers sense great indifference from their sons.
（關於母子關係，下列何者為真？→ 母親感受到兒子明顯的疏離。）
  • 定位：第一段「Most women writers stress the alienation between mothers and sons」＋「mothers discover to their astonishment that their sons have become a total stranger to them」。
  • 推論：alienation（疏離）與 total stranger（完全陌生）都指向兒子與母親的距離感，對應 (C) 的 indifference。
  • 其他選項：(A) 管教困難、(B) 孝道較少、(D) 對「媽寶」身分焦慮——文中都未提及。
  • ⚠️ (C) 的「indifference」與原文 alienation 略有落差，但為四個選項中最貼近者，請對照你的答案。
撇步
  • 細節題回文比對關鍵詞：alienation、stranger。

subItems.title: 23. Why is the mother-son separation a prevailing theme in contemporary women's writing?

options.text: Because mothers are advised to disconnect with their sons.
Because mothers feel obligated to attach themselves to their sons.
Because sons desire to strike a link with their mothers.
Because sons demonstrate resentment against their mothers.

subItems.hint:
→ Because mothers are advised to disconnect with their sons.
（為什麼母子分離是當代女性書寫的常見主題？→ 因為社會要求母親與兒子保持距離。）
  • 定位：第一段「since mothers are constrained by the society at large to avoid being too close to their sons in fear that they might smother their sons」。
  • 推論：社會約束母親不要與兒子太親近，否則會「寵壞、窒息」兒子——這就是「被要求保持距離」。
  • 其他選項：(B) 母親覺得有義務黏著兒子（相反）；(C) 兒子想建立連結（文中是疏離）；(D) 兒子表達怨恨（未提）。
撇步
  • 因果題抓 since／because 子句：constrained by society。

subItems.title: 24. How does Brown portray a mother who seems to be more compelling than that of Forster?

options.text: She makes a mother more dominant by monitoring everything her son does.
She allows a mother to work out the mother-son relationship on her own terms.
She enables a mother to embrace her selfhood by acting as a professional woman.
She creates a mother who knows how to rely on her knowledge to mold her son.

subItems.hint:
→ She allows a mother to work out the mother-son relationship on her own terms.
（Brown 如何刻畫一位比 Forster 筆下更有說服力的母親？→ 她讓母親依自己的方式處理母子關係。）
  • 定位：第二段「Brown describes a mother who exercises her agency and power to deal with her son's act of crime... decides her way of handling the mother-son separation.」
  • 對比：Forster 的母親是「passively accepting」傳統角色；Brown 的母親展現 agency（能動性）。
  • 其他選項：監控、職業女性、以知識塑造兒子——都不是文中描述。
撇步
  • 人物對比題抓關鍵詞：agency、her way（對比 passively accepting）。

subItems.title: 25. What is the actual meaning of the concluding sentence, “there exists a powerful reading and writing against the grain”?

options.text: It indicates that motherhood can be manipulative and nurturing.
It denotes that the social control of motherhood is severe and unexpected.
It argues that mothers have the authority to treat their children differently.
It illustrates that the act of mothering can go beyond the traditional script.

subItems.hint:
→ It illustrates that the act of mothering can go beyond the traditional script.
（「against the grain」這句結論的真正意思是？→ 母職可以跳脱傳統脚本。）
  • 片語：against the grain＝逆著紋理、反傳統、不順從常規。
  • 上下文：全文對比「Forster 的順從傳統」與「Brown 的展現能動性」，結論說兩種文本都顯示「存在一種強而有力的、逆潮流的閱讀與書寫」。
  • 其他選項：(A) 操縱與養育、(B) 社會控制嚴厲、(C) 母親有權差别對待——都不是「against the grain」的重點。
撇步
  • 片語題先確認字面義（逆紋理→反傳統），再對照全文對比。
